title: Geometric Frobenius acts on the Tate twist Lambda(m) by q^{-m}
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, $q=p^a$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ in $\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Take $Y_0=\Spec k_0$, so $Y=s=\Spec k$ and $g_s=\Spec(\gamma):s\to s$ with $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$ the geometric Frobenius. Let $\Lambda(m)_s$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, be the Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and $\theta_m:Lg_s^*\Lambda(m)_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(m)_s$ their canonical Weil structures [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Let

$$
 F_m:\RGamma(s,\Lambda(m)_s)\xrightarrow{\ \tau\ }\RGamma(s,Lg_s^*\Lambda(m)_s)\xrightarrow{\RGamma(\theta_m)}\RGamma(s,\Lambda(m)_s)
$$

be the geometric Frobenius endomorphism, $\tau$ being the transport of cohomology along $g_s$ [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] and $\RGamma$, $H^i$ the cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Then $H^i(s,\Lambda(m)_s)=0$ for $i\neq0$, $H^0(s,\Lambda(m)_s)$ is free of rank one over $\Lambda$, and $H^0(F_m)$ is multiplication by $q^{-m}$, where $q\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$ (as $\ell\neq p$) and $q^{-m}$ acts through $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\Lambda$. In particular geometric Frobenius acts on $\Lambda(1)$ by $q^{-1}$, on $\Lambda(m)$ by $q^{-m}$ and on $\Lambda(-d)$ by $q^{d}$ ($d\geq0$), for $\Lambda=E$ and $\Lambda=\Qlb$ (where this is the action of the global geometric Frobenius $F$ of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] on $H^0(s,E(m)_s)$, resp. its scalar extension to $\Qlb$). These scalars are compatible with finite reduction and scalar extension: the reduction isomorphism $H^0(s,\mathcal O_E(m)_s)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong H^0(s,A_{E,n}(m)_s)$, the isomorphism $H^0(s,\mathcal O_E(m)_s)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\cong H^0(s,E(m)_s)$ and the scalar-extension isomorphisms to $E'\supseteq E$ and to $\Qlb$ intertwine the operators $H^0(F_m)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-point-tate-root-coordinates] to choose $e$ and identify the finite and integral twist sections with $\Lambda e_{m,\Lambda}$. Since $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$, [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] identifies $\RGamma$ with the point fiber. Exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] give no cohomology outside degree zero. The rational and common-stage fiber formulas [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] extend these free lines to $E$ and $\Qlb$. Thus every stated $H^0$ is free of rank one.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E$, the transport normalization [lem-pur-point-frobenius-transport-normalization], applied to $M=\Lambda(m)_s$ and $v=\tau_m^\Lambda$, identifies the specified composite $F_m$ with $\Gamma(s,\tau_m^\Lambda)\sigma_{\Lambda(m)}$. Here $\theta_m=v\lambda_M$ is exactly the canonical Weil structure of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. The coordinate formula [lem-pur-point-signed-cyclotomic-action] therefore gives $F_m(b e_m)=bq^{-m}e_m$ for every integer $m$.

proof.text: The rational and common-stage transports are the images of the integral transport [lem-pur-point-frobenius-transport-normalization], and their Weil structures are the images of $\theta_m$ [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Consequently the same scalar acts after localization and at every finite stage of $\Qlb$. The canonical coefficient comparisons [lem-pur-point-tate-fiber-coefficient-comparisons] send $e_m\otimes b$ to $b e'_m$ and are transitive, including for dual generators. Via the point-fiber formulas [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] these are precisely the comparisons of the statement. For $u=q^{-m}$, each comparison $c$ satisfies $c((ux)\otimes b)=u\,c(x\otimes b)=F_m c(x\otimes b)$; the transitivity makes the $\Qlb$ equality independent of stage.

proof.text: The global operator of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] is the same transport-then-Weil-structure composite, so its $H^0$ action is the one computed above. Substitution of $m=1$ and $m=-d$ gives $q^{-1}$ and $q^d$, respectively.

proof.text: For the normalized scalarSheafLine_existsUnique helper, compose the inverse of the ordinary-to-completed tensor-model isomorphism of [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension] with twistLineScalarIso of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Its formula on local pure tensors is the required one; composing a competing map with the model isomorphism reduces uniqueness to twistLineScalarIso_existsUnique. The least coefficient embedding is constructed using Shrink.algEquiv and IntermediateField.botEquiv, and its uniqueness follows from injectivity of the embedding into the coefficient closure. The ordinary coefficient-size comparison and localization tensor comparison are natural linear equivalences built from ULift.moduleEquiv and TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.uliftEquiv/congr; pure tensors prove naturality and uniqueness. IntegralPointSections_eq is definitional after unfolding the unchanged-object rationalization and integral operation wrappers. These helper proofs leave the four main assembly steps above unchanged.

For the derived reduction helper, the integral first Tate line is locally free of rank one, so coefficientTwistLine_exact makes every signed line flat. FlatSingleDerivedNormalization makes its degree-zero single complex K-flat. The universal reduction counit of integralReductionTowerWellDefinedUnrestricted is therefore invertible. Compose it with the single-complex comparison and reductionSheafLine. The defining equality specifies its hom literally, hence uniqueness follows by Iso.ext.

Cancel that isomorphism to see that the specified counit is invertible. Convert the intrinsic completeness included in integralLine.property to legacy completeness using sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy with an auxiliary finite-field datum in universe zero. finiteFreeCompletedScalarComparison makes the specified completion comparison chi invertible. Compose chi inverse, the ordinary scalar counit, the single-complex comparison, and single.mapIso scalarSheafLine. The proved generic isoFactor_existsUnique lemma gives the defining equation and uniqueness by categorical cancellation. No coefficient map or line normalization is changed.

proof.text: The four independently stated component theorems provide the finite/integral, rational/common-stage, reduction/localization, and field-extension conjuncts. Conjunction introduction assembles them into the displayed target without changing any statement.

For signedQuotients_existsUnique, first generalize the geometric point to an arbitrary scheme S (no property of the point is needed for this helper). Construct normalized quotient isomorphisms on every nonnegative tensor power using signedTwistFirstReduction and induction with the unit and binary scalar-extension isomorphisms of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence]. The existing private positiveComparison construction in SignedLineScalarTensorTower implements precisely this induction without a rank-one hypothesis; the signed comparison theorem is not applied. Their units form an AdicPurityRootQuotients family: the coefficient formula proves degree zero, the first-root quotient formula proves degree one on original root tensors, and the tensor formula proves the recursion. Uniqueness of adicPurityRootQuotients identifies this family with the specified nonnegative maps. For a negative exponent, extend the positive-power functional by scalarDualBaseMap and precompose with the inverse positive-power isomorphism. Its evaluation on the positive quotient is the coefficient projection of the original evaluation. To compare two such negative maps, precompose with the positive-power isomorphism on each slice and test on scalar-extension pure tensors. Naturality reduces arbitrary slice evaluations to identity slices, where the prescribed evaluation equation applies; scalar linearity treats the extra quotient scalar. This proves uniqueness of the entire signed family. No invertibility of l on the scheme, root basis, or flatness of the quotient coefficient map is needed for this helper.
